name: Yolk-Forward Herb Scramble
blurb: Egg white is the problem, not the egg. Six yolks and a knob of butter give you a scramble that scores clean.
steps: Whisk the yolks with the cream and a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter in a cold pan over low heat.
Add the yolks and stir constantly with a spatula — low and slow, 3–4 minutes, until barely set.
Off the heat, fold in the chives and eat immediately.
tip: Save the whites for something else, or discard them. SIGHI scores egg white 2 and flags it as a mast-cell liberator even cooked.

name: Ricotta and Blueberry Bowl
blurb: Fresh unripened cheese is the one dairy category that stays at zero. Five minutes, no cooking.
steps: Spoon the ricotta into a bowl and loosen it with a fork.
Top with blueberries, chia, coconut and cinnamon.
Eat within the hour — opened ricotta climbs quickly.
tip: Check the tub date. Fresh cheeses score 0 while sealed and fresh; the same ricotta at day six is a different food.

name: Overnight Coconut-Chia Pudding
blurb: The one make-ahead that is safe: nothing is cooked, so nothing is accumulating histamine as a leftover.
steps: Stir chia into the coconut milk with the vanilla.
Rest 10 minutes, stir again to break up clumps, then refrigerate overnight.
Top with blueberries and pumpkin seeds to serve.
tip: Uncooked, sealed and cold, this holds two days. Cooked leftovers would not.

name: Turkey and Zucchini Breakfast Patties
blurb: Grind the turkey yourself or buy it ground to order. Pre-packed ground meat is the hidden score-2 in most breakfasts.

ingredients.display: zucchini, peeled, deseeded, grated and squeezed dry

steps: Mix the turkey, squeezed zucchini, herbs and salt. Do not overwork it.
Form six flat patties.
Sear in olive oil over medium heat, 3–4 minutes a side, until cooked through.
Serve straight from the pan.
tip: Any patties you will not eat now go into the freezer hot-cooled, not the fridge.

name: Cream Cheese Pancakes
blurb: Yolks, cream cheese and a little almond flour. No banana, no aged dairy, no wheat.
steps: Blend the cream cheese, yolks, almond flour and cinnamon until smooth.
Rest the batter 3 minutes.
Cook silver-dollar rounds in butter over medium-low, 2 minutes a side.
Serve with blueberries.
tip: Almond scores 1 — this is an 'allow 1' dish. At a strict-0 ceiling, drop the almond flour and add a tablespoon of coconut flour instead.

name: Fresh Beef and Sweet Potato Hash
blurb: The higher-carb breakfast, for a training day. Sweet potato scores 0 and behaves.
steps: Fry the sweet potato in olive oil over medium heat, covered, 10 minutes until tender.
Add the onion, cook 3 minutes.
Push aside, brown the beef hard in the same pan, then combine.
Finish with paprika, salt and parsley.
tip: White onion scores 0 where yellow and red onion score 1 — worth keeping the white on hand.

name: Lettuce-Wrapped Smash Burgers
blurb: No bun, no ketchup, no aged cheese, no pickle. Everything that normally makes a burger a problem, removed.
steps: Divide the beef into four loose balls. Do not salt yet.
Get a heavy pan smoking hot with the butter.
Smash each ball flat, salt the top, sear 90 seconds, flip, 60 seconds more.
Lay mozzarella on to soften, then build in the lettuce leaves with cucumber and onion.
tip: Fresh mozzarella scores 0 where every aged cheese scores 2 or 3. It is the burger cheese for this diet.

name: Sheet-Pan Chicken with Fennel and Carrot
blurb: One tray, four ingredients that all score zero, and enough for the next day if you freeze it hot.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss fennel and carrot with 2 tbsp oil and salt on a sheet pan.
Rub the chicken with the remaining oil and salt, set it skin-up on the vegetables, tuck rosemary underneath.
Roast 35–40 minutes until the skin is crisp and the thigh reads 175°F.
tip: Portion any surplus into the freezer while the pan is still warm. Refrigerated overnight, this becomes a score-2 meal.

name: Cod in Brown Butter with Parsley
blurb: Frozen-at-sea white fish is the safest protein on the list. Counter fish is one of the worst.
steps: Thaw the cod in the fridge and pat it very dry. Salt it.
Sear in 1 tbsp butter over medium-high, 3 minutes a side. Lift out.
Add the remaining butter, swirl until it smells nutty and turns amber.
Wilt the zucchini ribbons in the butter for a minute, spoon over the fish with the parsley.
tip: No lemon. Citrus scores 2 and is a liberator — the brown butter is doing the acid's job here.

name: Cauliflower Rice Bowl with Ricotta and Basil
blurb: A no-protein lunch that still holds together, built on two score-zero ingredients.
steps: Pulse the cauliflower to rice in a food processor.
Fry it in olive oil over high heat, 6–7 minutes, undisturbed at first so it browns.
Steam or blanch the broccoli 3 minutes and fold it in.
Top with ricotta, torn basil, pumpkin seeds and salt.
tip: Pumpkin seeds score 0 where most nuts score 1 to 3 — they are the crunch to keep in the pantry.

name: Turkey Lettuce Cups with Cucumber and Dill
blurb: The lunch to make when you refuse to cook. No deli meat — deli turkey scores 3.
steps: Loosen the cream cheese with a splash of water into a spoonable dressing. Fold in dill and chives.
Dice the turkey and toss with the cucumber and dressing.
Spoon into lettuce cups and salt.
tip: This is the honest reason to roast a whole turkey breast on Sunday and freeze it in portions — sliced deli turkey is a score-3 food.

name: Zucchini Noodles, Basil and Pumpkin Seed Pesto
blurb: Pesto without pine nuts, parmesan or lemon — three ingredients this diet cannot have.
steps: Blitz basil, pumpkin seeds, olive oil and salt to a coarse pesto. Blend in the ricotta last.
Salt the zucchini noodles, rest 10 minutes, squeeze dry.
Warm the noodles 90 seconds in a dry hot pan — no longer, or they weep.
Toss with the pesto off the heat. Add sliced seared chicken if you want the protein.
tip: Parmesan is a matured hard cheese: score 3. Ricotta carries the creaminess at score 0.

name: Trout with Cucumber and Mint
blurb: Freshwater trout is one of the few fish SIGHI rates at zero outright.
steps: Salt the trout and sear skin-down in olive oil, 4 minutes, then 1 minute on the flesh side.
Toss cucumber ribbons, radish and mint with the cream and a pinch of salt.
Plate the salad cold under the hot fish.
tip: No vinegar in the salad — every vinegar except distilled white scores 2 or higher, and even that one is disputed.

name: Herb-Roasted Chicken with Asparagus
blurb: The Sunday anchor. Roast it, eat it, freeze the rest in portions the same evening.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Work the butter, thyme and chopped sage under the skin. Salt the bird generously.
Roast 50 minutes, or until the thigh reads 175°F.
Toss asparagus in olive oil and salt, add to the pan for the last 12 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes and carve.
tip: Freeze leftover meat within an hour of carving. Chicken kept in the fridge overnight is no longer a score-0 food.

name: Pan-Seared Cod with Fennel and Leek
blurb: Braised fennel and leek give you the sweetness that would normally come from onion or tomato.
steps: Sweat the fennel and leek in butter over low heat, covered, 12 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the cream and thyme, simmer 3 minutes.
Salt the cod, sear it separately in a hot dry pan 3 minutes a side.
Spoon the fennel cream onto the plate and set the cod on top.
tip: Leek scores 1 — swap in a second fennel bulb for a strict-0 version.

name: Lamb Chops with Rosemary and Zucchini
blurb: Fresh unaged lamb scores 0. Dry-aged anything scores 3 — ask what you are buying.
steps: Salt the chops 20 minutes ahead and bring them to room temperature.
Sear in olive oil over high heat, 3 minutes a side for medium-rare. Add rosemary and butter for the last minute and baste.
Rest 5 minutes.
Char the zucchini in the same pan while the meat rests.
tip: Dry-aged beef and lamb are score 3. The word on the label to avoid is 'aged', not 'grass-fed'.

name: Beef and Cabbage Skillet
blurb: Cabbage raw and cooked is a zero. Cabbage fermented is a three. Same vegetable, opposite ends of the scale.
steps: Brown the beef hard in butter, breaking it up. Remove.
Cook the onion and cabbage in the fat, 10 minutes, until the edges catch.
Add the caraway, return the beef, salt well.
Finish with parsley off the heat.
tip: Caraway carries the sauerkraut flavour without the fermentation — a useful substitution to remember.

name: Sea Bass en Papillote with Carrot and Thyme
blurb: Steaming in paper keeps everything moist without a sauce built on wine, stock or citrus.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Build two parchment parcels: carrot and fennel first, fish on top, salt, thyme, a knob of butter.
Fold the paper tightly closed and bake 14 minutes.
Open at the table — the steam is the point.
tip: Long-simmered bone broth and stock cubes both score 2. Papillote is how you get moisture without either.

name: Veal with Sage and Brown Butter
blurb: Saltimbocca minus the prosciutto — the ham is what would have made it a score-3 plate.
steps: Press a sage leaf onto each side of the cutlets and salt them.
Sear in olive oil, 90 seconds a side. Remove.
Brown the butter in the pan, crisp the remaining sage leaves in it, pour over the veal.
Blanch the green beans 4 minutes and dress with a little of the same butter.
tip: Green beans score 1 — swap to asparagus or broccoli for a strict-0 plate.

name: Turkey Meatballs in Basil Cream
blurb: The tomato-sauce shape without the tomato — tomato is both high-histamine and a liberator.
steps: Mix turkey, ricotta, yolk, half the basil and salt. Roll into 18 balls.
Brown them in olive oil, turning, about 6 minutes. Remove.
Soften the onion in the pan, add the cream, simmer 5 minutes to thicken.
Return the meatballs, cover, 8 minutes. Blitz or tear in the remaining basil.
Serve over warmed zucchini noodles.
tip: Breadcrumbs would push this off keto and add a score-1 grain; ricotta binds just as well.

name: Duck Breast with Braised Red Cabbage
blurb: The 'special occasion' plate that stays inside the rules. Red cabbage braised in apple, not vinegar.
steps: Score the duck fat in a crosshatch and salt it. Start it fat-down in a cold pan over medium-low; render 10–12 minutes until the skin is glassy.
Flip, 4 minutes. Rest 8 minutes.
Meanwhile braise the cabbage with the apple, cloves, butter, salt and a splash of water, covered, 25 minutes.
Slice the duck and serve over the cabbage.
tip: Braised red cabbage is normally finished with vinegar. Grated apple does the same job at score 0.

name: Pollock and Potato Chowder
blurb: A creamy bowl built without stock cubes, bacon or canned corn — all of which score 2 or 3.
steps: Sweat the leek and carrot in butter, 6 minutes.
Add the potato, milk and enough water to cover. Simmer 15 minutes until tender.
Add the cream, then the fish in large pieces. Poach 5 minutes off a hard boil.
Salt, finish with dill, serve immediately.
tip: Do not refrigerate this. Freeze any surplus straight away in single portions.

name: Roasted Broccoli with Garlic Butter
blurb: The side that goes with everything on this list.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the florets with olive oil and salt, spread on a hot tray, roast 18 minutes until the edges char.
Melt the butter with crushed garlic off the heat, pour over.
tip: Garlic scores 1. Leave it out and finish with parsley for a strict-0 side.

name: Cauliflower Mash with Ghee
blurb: Ghee and quark do the work that sour cream or aged parmesan usually would.
steps: Steam the cauliflower 12 minutes until completely soft.
Drain very well — wet cauliflower makes a loose mash.
Blend with ghee, quark and salt until silky.
Fold in chives.
tip: Sour cream scores 1 because it is cultured; quark stays at 0.

name: Cucumber and Radish Salad with Dill Cream
blurb: A cold side with no vinegar and no lemon in it — harder to find than it sounds.
steps: Salt the cucumber slices and rest 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Whisk the cream with dill, chives and a pinch of salt until slightly thickened.
Fold everything together and serve cold.
tip: The salt-and-rest step gives you the snap that vinegar normally provides.

name: Macadamia and Coconut Fat Bombs
blurb: Macadamia is one of only three nuts that score 0. Walnut and mixed nuts score 3.
steps: Blitz the macadamias to a coarse butter.
Melt the coconut oil and blend it in with the vanilla and salt.
Fold in the shredded coconut, spoon into a mini muffin tray, freeze 30 minutes.
Keep them in the freezer, not the fridge.
tip: Macadamia, Brazil nut and pistachio are the score-0 nuts. Everything labelled 'mixed nuts' is a 3.

name: Blueberry Mascarpone Cups
blurb: Dessert that scores zero. Strawberries and raspberries would not — both are liberators at score 2.
steps: Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it into the mascarpone with the vanilla.
Layer with blueberries and blackberries in two glasses.
Chill 20 minutes, no longer.
tip: Blueberry, blackberry, redcurrant and cranberry all score 0. Strawberry and raspberry score 2.

name: Pumpkin Seed and Coconut Trail Mix
blurb: The bag to keep in the car so a gas-station snack never becomes the decision.
steps: Toss everything with the melted coconut oil.
Spread on a tray and toast at 325°F for 8–10 minutes, stirring once.
Cool completely before bagging, or it will steam and go soft.
tip: Dried fruit is sulphured and scores 2, so this mix stays savoury.

name: Quinoa Bowl with Chicken and Roast Carrot
blurb: The refeed-day bowl. Quinoa, rice and millet are the score-0 grains.

ingredients.display: quinoa, rinsed until the water runs clear

steps: Rinse the quinoa well, simmer in salted water 15 minutes, drain and steam-dry.
Roast the carrots in oil and salt at 425°F for 22 minutes.
Sear the chicken, rest, slice.
Build the bowl and finish with parsley, pumpkin seeds and the remaining olive oil.
tip: Buckwheat looks like a safe pseudo-grain but scores 2. Quinoa, millet, amaranth and rice are the safe ones.

name: Oat Porridge with Blueberry and Coconut
blurb: When you want carbs at breakfast: oats score 0, and so does everything on top of them here.
steps: Simmer the oats in the milk with a pinch of salt, 6–8 minutes, stirring.
Off the heat, stir in the cinnamon.
Top with blueberries and coconut.
tip: Banana would be the obvious topping and scores 2. Blueberries and cooked apple are the swaps.

name: Quail Egg and Mozzarella Skillet
blurb: Quail eggs score 0 whole, where a whole chicken egg scores 2. The simplest way to eat a real egg breakfast.
steps: Melt the butter in a small skillet over medium-low heat.
Crack the quail eggs in around the pan and scatter the mozzarella between them.
Cover for 3 minutes until the whites set and the cheese slumps.
Salt, tear over the basil, eat from the pan.
tip: Whole chicken egg scores 2 because of the white; quail eggs are rated 0 whole.

name: Whipped Cream Cheese with Blackberry
blurb: Two minutes of whisking turns cream cheese into something that feels like a dessert at breakfast.
steps: Whisk the cream into the cream cheese until light and spoonable.
Crush half the blackberries through it, leave the rest whole on top.
Finish with coconut, chia and cinnamon.
tip: Blackberry, blueberry, redcurrant and cranberry are the score-0 berries.

name: Seared Steak with Charred Zucchini
blurb: Fresh unaged beef, cooked and eaten inside ten minutes. The most reliably clean plate there is, at any hour.
steps: Salt the steak and get a heavy pan very hot with the olive oil.
Sear 2½ minutes a side, adding butter and thyme for the last minute to baste.
Rest the steak 5 minutes; char the zucchini in the same pan while it rests.
Slice against the grain and eat straight away.
tip: Ask the butcher whether the beef is dry-aged. Aged beef scores 3 no matter how fresh it looks.

name: Curd Cheese with Cucumber and Radish
blurb: The four-o'clock snack that needs no cooking and nothing from a jar.
steps: Fold the cucumber and radish through the curd cheese.
Salt, add the parsley, and drizzle the olive oil over the top.
tip: Quark, curd cheese and cottage cheese all score 0 — the unripened fresh cheeses are your safe dairy.

name: Roasted Cauliflower with Sweet Paprika
blurb: Sweet paprika scores 0 where hot paprika, cayenne, black pepper and curry powder all score 2.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the florets with oil, paprika and salt.
Roast 25 minutes on a hot tray, turning once, until deeply browned at the edges.
Scatter parsley over before serving.
tip: If a recipe calls for black pepper, sweet paprika is usually the substitution that works.

name: Coconut and Pumpkin Seed Bark
blurb: Chocolate is out — cocoa contains theobromine, a DAO blocker. This is what replaces it.
steps: Melt the coconut oil gently and stir in the cinnamon.
Mix in the coconut flakes, pumpkin seeds and macadamia.
Spread thin on a lined tray and freeze 25 minutes until solid.
Break into shards and keep in the freezer.
tip: Cocoa and chocolate carry theobromine, which blocks DAO. This is the swap that keeps the ritual.

name: Ghee-Fried Yolks with Asparagus
blurb: Zero on both scales. Egg yolk, ghee and asparagus have neither histamine nor lectin to speak of.
steps: Melt the ghee in a small pan over low heat.
Slide the yolks in whole and cook 2 minutes, basting, until just warmed through and still liquid.
Sear the asparagus in the same pan, 4 minutes, until blistered.
Salt, scatter thyme, serve.
tip: Ghee rather than butter: clarifying removes the milk protein, which is what carries the A1 casein concern.

name: Mascarpone and Blackberry Cup
blurb: The cleanest sweet thing on the list — blackberries score 0 on both scales, mascarpone 1 on lectin.
steps: Loosen the mascarpone with a fork.
Fold half the blackberries through it, leaving the rest whole on top.
Finish with coconut and cinnamon.
tip: Chia would normally go here but scores 2 for lectin. Shredded coconut does the same job at 0.

name: Coconut and Hemp Breakfast Bowl
blurb: Hemp seed is the one seed that clears both scales at zero. No chia, no pumpkin seed, no oats.
steps: Stir the hemp seeds into the coconut milk and let them sit 5 minutes to soften.
Top with blueberries, macadamia and cinnamon.
tip: Pumpkin and chia seeds both score 2 for lectin despite being histamine-clean. Hemp is the swap.

name: Chicken and Kale Skillet
blurb: Kale, white onion and fresh chicken are all zero on both scales — no prep workaround needed.
steps: Salt the chicken and sear skin-side down in olive oil, 7 minutes, until deeply browned. Flip, 5 minutes more. Remove.
Soften the onion in the fat, 5 minutes.
Add the kale in handfuls, wilting each before the next, 4 minutes.
Return the chicken, scatter rosemary, salt, serve from the pan.
tip: White onion is 0 for histamine where yellow and red are 1, and 0 for lectin either way.

name: Cod with Braised Cabbage and Fennel
blurb: A whole plate at zero on both scales. Nothing here needs peeling, deseeding or pressure-cooking.
steps: Braise the cabbage and fennel in ghee with the caraway, covered, over low heat, 15 minutes.
Salt the cod and sear it separately in a hot dry pan, 3 minutes a side.
Bed the fish on the cabbage and finish with parsley.
tip: Fennel and cabbage are the two most reliable vegetables when you are running both protocols at once.

name: Lamb Chops with Artichoke and Mint
blurb: Artichoke is one of the few substantial vegetables that clears both scales without preparation tricks.
steps: Salt the chops and bring them to room temperature.
Steam or braise the artichoke hearts until tender, 15 minutes, then halve and brown them in olive oil.
Sear the chops over high heat, 3 minutes a side, with the rosemary in the pan.
Rest 5 minutes, plate with the artichoke, and tear over the mint.
tip: Jarred artichoke hearts are packed in vinegar and score 3 for histamine. Fresh or frozen only.

name: Roasted Fennel with Olive Oil
blurb: The default side when both scores have to be zero. Sweet paprika is out — it is a nightshade.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the fennel wedges in oil, salt and oregano.
Roast 25 minutes, turning once, until the edges caramelise.
Finish with parsley.
tip: Sweet paprika is histamine-clean at 0 but scores 2 for lectin — it is dried nightshade. Oregano replaces it here.

name: Macadamia and Coconut Clusters
blurb: Zero on both scales. Macadamia is one of only a handful of nuts that clears histamine and lectin at once.
steps: Roughly chop half the macadamias and leave the rest whole.
Melt the coconut oil with the cinnamon and salt.
Stir everything together, spoon into a lined tray in small mounds, freeze 25 minutes.
Keep them in the freezer.
tip: Pumpkin seeds appear in the older version of this and score 2 for lectin. Straight macadamia keeps it at 0.

name: Celery and Radish with Ghee Salt
blurb: Two minutes, nothing cooked, both scores at zero. The snack for when nothing else qualifies.
steps: Whip the softened ghee with the salt and chopped parsley.
Serve the celery and radish alongside for dipping.
tip: Hummus would be the obvious dip and scores 2 for histamine and 3 for lectin. Whipped ghee is the replacement.

name: Beef and Brussels Sprout Hash
blurb: The savoury breakfast when the lectin ceiling is tight — no zucchini, no sweet potato, no nightshade.
steps: Brown the beef hard in ghee, breaking it up. Remove.
Cook the onion and shredded sprouts in the fat, 8 minutes, until the cut edges catch.
Return the beef with the caraway, salt well.
Finish with parsley off the heat.
tip: Brussels sprouts score 1 for histamine and 0 for lectin — the trade that makes this an 'allow 1' dish.
